Shafique Ahmed with KB Rumy, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Md. Yeasin Khan, Advocate ------ For the Respondent Nos. 2 and 3. 
Md. Sagir Hossain, Advocate ------ For the Respondent No. 11.
parties:
Noruzzaman Sarker ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by its Secretary, Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development (LGRD), Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Quazi Rezaul Hoque, J: The instant Rule was issued on 12-6-2016 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the letter being Memo No. 17.00.68.64.035.46.093.14.215 dated 17-5-2016 signed by the respondent No. 4 containing an order of stay the publication of gazette of the result of the Chorarlia Union Parishad Election, Raypura, Narsingdi held on 7-5-2016, and to conduct an investigation (annexure- E) should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. At the time of issuance of the Rule there were two interim order to the effect that the operation of the letter being Memo No. 17.00.68.64.035.46.093.14.215 dated 17-5-2016 signed by the respondent No. 4 (annexure- E) was stayed for a period of 06(six) months from date and the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 were directed to publish the name of the petitioner as elected Chairman of Chorarlia Union Parishad, Raypura, Narsingdi in the form of Gazette Notification as per Rule-43 of the “স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০.” And the Appellate Division vide order dated 21-8-2016, stayed operation of the interim order of stay and direction till disposal of the Rule.

2. The core contention with regard to the instant Rule is an election of an Union Parishad at Choraralia Union Parishad, Raypura, Narsingdi. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, as has been stated the petitioner the that the respondents No. 10 i.e. the returning officer circulated a circular containing election schedule for the Election of Choraralia Union Parishad by Memo No. “৪৭.৬২.৬৪.৬৮.০০০.০০.০০১.১৬-৬৩ তারিখ ২৮-৩-২০১৬” (annexure-A). In accordance with the said circular, the last date of submitting nomination paper was fixed on 7-4-2016 date of scrutinizing the nomination paper was fixed on 10-4-2016 and 11-4-2016, the date of withdrawing of the candidate was fixed on 18-4-2016 and date of election was fixed on 7-5-2016.

3. Thereafter the instant petitioner got nomination from Bangladesh Awami League on  6-4-2016 to participate in the Union Parishad Election of District, Narsingdi Upazila—Raypura, Union Parishad—Choraralia as a Chairman candidate (annexure-B). And thereafter on 7-4-2016, the instant petitioner as a candidate of the Election for the post of Chairman Choraralia, Raypura, Narsingdi complying all the necessary formalities, submitted his nomination paper with affidavit to the returning officer and receiving the said nomination paper, the returning officer provided the petitioner the acknowledgement receipt on 7-4-2016 (annexure- C).

4. After completing all the formalities required the respondent No. 10 i.e. the returning officer on 11-4-2016 declared the instant writ petitioner as a valid candidate of the said election and thereafter on 19-4-2016 the returning officer allotted him the symbol of boat (নৌকা) to participate on the said election.

5. Thereafter the election was held on 7-5-2016 peacefully and without any hindrance from any vested quarter and consequently no complain was made to any single presiding officer of any centre or to any other authorized person by any candidate, either at the time of the election or after the completion of the said election as per the knowledge of the petitioner.

6. After counting the votes peacefully every presiding officer took signatures of the agents of the candidates on the result sheets and delivered the result sheets to them and declared the result of their own centres in presence of the agents in presence of the agents of the candidates. Later the presiding officers sent the records, including the result sheets to the returning officer and afterwards the returning officer gave written notice to every contesting candidate and their agents to be present at a particular place in a fixed time in order to consolidate the results sent by the presiding officers. Thereafter on 7-5-2016, the respondent No. 10 i.e. the returning officer consolidating the results in presence of the contesting candidates or their agents declaring the votes of the contesting candidates and finally declared the instant petitioner elected as a Chairman whereas the instant petitioner got in total 5048 votes in the symbol of boat (নৌকা) and the contesting candidate got in total 3285 votes in the symbol of ধানের শীষ.

7. The respondent No. 10 i.e. the returning officer circulated the results by public circular and as per the said result sheet in the Baghaikandi Purba Para Furkania Madrasa centre the instant petitioner got 211 votes and the contesting candidate got 489 votes, in the community centre the petitioner got 325 votes and the contesting candidate got 378 votes, in the Baghaikandi Government Primary School Centre the petitioner got 165 votes and the contesting candidate got 1179 votes, in the Chorararia Government Primary School Centre the petitioner got 459 votes and the contesting candidate got 900 votes in the Bordahandi Government Primary School centre the petitioner got 120 votes and the contesting candidate got 336 votes, in the Batakandi Government Primary School centre the petitioner got 843 votes and the contesting candidate got vote, in the Bottuli Government Primary School centre the petitioner got 1073 votes and the contesting candidate got 03 vote, in the Khamarpara Madrasa centre the petitioner got 893 votes and the contesting candidate got 0 vote, in the Bottuli Khamar Government Primary School centre the petitioner got 959 votes and the contesting candidate got 0 vote. Thereafter the returning officer provided the attested result sheets containing in the form "ঠ" to all the candidates and/or their agents as per the rule 42 (6) of the local Government Union Parishad Rules 2010 (annexure-D).

8. Later the instant petitioner was informed by a reliable source that a contesting candidate submitted an application on 9-5-206 i.e. after 2 days of the election to the Election Commissions of Bangladesh, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka demanding re-election.

9. Afterwards the petitioner got informed and thereby collected a letter being Memo No. ১৭.০০.৬৮৬৪.০৩৫.৪৬.০৯৩.১৪-২১৫ তারিখঃ ১৭-৫-২০১৬ singed by the respondent No. 4 i.e. the Senior Assistant Secretary (জঃব্যঃ-২) Election Commission, Bangladesh containing an order of stay of the publication of Gazette of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election, held on 7-5-2016 of Raypura Narsingdi and to conduct an investigation about the allegation made by a contesting candidate (annexure-E).

10. Though the respondent No. 2 i.e. the Election Commission is bound to publish the result in the form of Gazette notification but in the instant case, the Gazette publication of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election 2016 was stayed by the election commission which is ex facie illegal mala fide and without jurisdiction.

11. The petitioner had not been informed by the authority about the said letter being Memo No. ১৭.০০.৬৮৬৪.০৩৫.৪৬.০৯৩.১৪-২১৫ তারিখঃ ১৭-৫-২০১৬ though he is the elected Chairman of Choraralia Union Parishad and subsequently the investigation officers have not informed or sent any notice to the petitioner about the said investigation, therefore, the petitioner is completely in dark about the activities of the concerned investigation officers.

12. The respondent Nos. 2 and 3 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that the election was held on 7-5-2016.

13. It is stated that according to the statement recorded by the Regional Election Officer, Dhaka the contesting Chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzaman was complaining from the beginning of poll about serious illegalities and irregularities in voting of Chararalia Union Parishad Election 2016 for the post of Chairman candidate to the concerned Returning Officer, Upazila Election Officer and District Election Officer through mobile phone and on the same day i.e. 7-5-2016 at 1-00 pm he filed a written complain to the Election Commission through the District Election Officer, Narsingdi and on 9-5-2016 he filed a written complain to the Election Commission through the District Election Officer, Narsingdi and on 9-5-2016 he filed another written complain to the Chief Election Commission for staying election result and demanding re-election. The Election Commission took decision to stay publication of the election result by Gazette notification and ordered Mihir Sarwar Morshed, Regional Election Officer Dhaka to hold inquiry and to submit report by 25-5-2016 vide impugned letter (annexure-E) to the writ petition and the Regional Election Officer after recording statements and collecting information from the complainant, the writ petitioner, the Returning Officer, Presiding Officers Assistant Presiding Officers, Polling Officers, Member Candidate, Officer-in-charge of Raypura Police Station, Officers-in- charge of Law Enforcing agencies of the respective election centres, Upazila Nirbahi Officer of Raypura Narsingdi, District Election Officer of Narsingdi and Upazila Election Officer of Raypura, Narsingdi has submitted his report to the Election Commission Secretariat on 1-6-2016, from which it clearly appears that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provisions of law, and rules in 4 (four) centres of Choraralia Union Parishad Election 2016 held on 7-5-2016 (annexure-2, 3 and 4 respectively).

14. After counting the votes peacefully, every presiding officer took signatures of the  agents of the candidates on the result sheets and delivered the result sheet and declared the result of their own centres in presence of the agents of the candidates. The Returning Officer gave written notice to every candidates and their agents to be present at particular place in a fixed time in order to consolidate and the result sent by the presiding officers and on 7-5-2016 the Returning Officer consolidating the result in presence of the contesting candidate or their agents declaring the votes of the contesting candidates and finally declared the petitioner as Chairman, whereas the petitioner got in total 5048 votes and the contesting candidate got in total 3285 votes are not correct. It is stated that after receiving complaints from the contesting Chairman candidate Md. Hasanuzzaman about serious illegalities in voting in 4 centres to the Election Officer, Dhaka was directed to hold inquiry and to submit report by 25-5-2016 vide impugned letter (annexure-E) and the Regional Election Commission Secretariat on 1-6-2016 from which it clearly appears that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provision of law and rules in 4 (four) centres of Choraralia Union Parishad 2016 held on 7-5-2016.

15. It appears from the inquiry report submitted by the Regional Election Officer on 1-6-2016 that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provisions of law, and rules in 4 (four) centres of Choraralia Union Parishad Election 2016 held on 7-5-2016 and, as such, the result circulated by the returning officers was not a correct reflection of the scenario of the election held on 7-5-2016 in the said 4 (four) disputed centres of Choraralia Union Parishad Election, Raypura, Narsingdi.

16. The instant petitioner was informed by a reliable source that a contesting candidate submitted an application on 9-5-2016 i.e. after 2 days of the election to the Election Commission Bangladesh, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka demanding re-election are not correct as the contesting Chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman filed a written complain to the election Commission through the District Election Officer, Narsingdi on 7-5-2016 at 1-00 PM i.e. on the election day and thereafter again on 9-5-2016 to the Chief Election Commission for staying Election result and demanding re-election.

17. The Election Commission in exercise of plenary and supervisory power can act upon the post-election dispute and on the basis of complaints of the contesting Chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman about illegalities and irregularities in voting of 4 (four) election centres, the Election Commission took decision to stay publication of the election result by Gazette notification and ordered the regional Election Officer to hold inquiry and to submit report by 25-5-2016 vide impugned letter (annexure-E) and the Regional Election Officer, Dhaka after due inquiry has submitted his report to the Election Commission on 1-6-2016, from which it clearly appears that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provision of law, and Rules in 4 (four) centres of Chorarali Union Parishad Election 2016 held on 7-5-2016.

18. The Election Commission Secretariat on 1-6-2016 from which it clearly appears that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provisions of law and rules 4 (four) centres of Choraralia Union Parishad Election 2016 held on 7-5-2016 now, the Election Commission, in exercise of its plenary and supervisory power under Article 119 (2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh read with section 20 and 21 of the Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2009 and Rule 43 and 90 of the Local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 is under Constitutional and lawful obligation to decide and proceed with the matter on the basis of the merit of the investigation report.

19. The petitioner had not been informed by the authority about the said letter being Memo No. ১৭.০০.৬৮৬৪.০৩৫.৪৬.০৯৩.১৪-২১৫ তারিখঃ ১৭-৫-২০১৬ though he is the elected Chairman of Choraralia Union Parishad and subsequently the investigation officers have not informed or sent any notice to the petitioner about the said investigation and therefore, the petitioner was completely in dark about the activities of the concerned investigation officers are not correct. During investigation, the Regional Election Officer, Dhaka informed the petitioner and others and recorded their statements and collected information from them by open hearing on 22-5-2016 when the petitioner and his rival chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman were duly present by signing in a printed attendance sheet form and thereafter the Regional Election Officer submitted his report on 1-6-2016 but the petitioner, suppressing such facts, after submission of the investigation report have filed the petition on 9-6-2016 (annexure-5).

20. In exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 119(2) of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh read with section 20 and 21 of the Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2009 and Rule 43 and 90 of the local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 the Election Commission is empowered with plenary and supervisory power to conduct the Union Parishad Election freely, fairly justly and honestly, which covers the entire process that starts with the publication of the notification of schedule and culminates with the publication of the result in the official Gazette and section 21 of the Local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 and before publication of the election result in the official Gazette under Rule 43 of the local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 the Election Commission in exercise of plenary and supervisory power can act upon the post-election dispute, therefore, Election Commission committed no illegality in issuing the impugned Memo on the basis of complain of the contesting Chairman candidate Md Hasanuzzaman about illegalities and irregularities of voting in 4 (four) election centres on the very day of the election on 7-5-2016 and thereafter again on 9-5-2016 the Election Commission also took the decision with lawful authority to stay publication of the disputed election result.

21. It is stated that during investigation the Regional Election Officer, Dhaka informed the petitioner and others and recorded their statements and collected information from them by open hearing on 22-5-2016 when the writ petitioner and his rival Chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman were duly present by the signing in a printed attendance sheet form and thereafter the Regional Election Officer submitted his report on 1-6-2016, but he petitioner suppressing such facts, after submission of the investigation report have filed this petition on 9-6-2016, therefore, the Rule is not maintainable as being infructuous.

22. The respondent No. 11 contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition con-tending inter rain that the petitioner by hindrance, exercising colourable power imposing power entered in to the voting centre on 7-5-2016 and cast the votes in favour of him by rigging in 4 (four) vote centres, the petitioner cast all votes including the votes of dead persons and of those who are out of the country.

23. The added respondent No. 11 the returning officer and the presiding officers of ward Nos. 6-9 in collusion with the petitioner by exercising colourable power sealed in the symbol of Boat Nouka and attested result sheet under form No. Da, which was not a free and fair election result.

24. Since the presiding officers of ward Nos. 6-9 had not conducted the election free and fair in which 100% votes was cast in favour of the petitioner. It is not possible in any election where thousands of people are voters and to cast 100% votes, so the election commission investigated and stopped publishing Gazette Notification by Memo dated 17-5-2016.

25. The memo dated was issued on 17-5-2016 and the Gazette was stayed till 25-5-2016 but the petition was filed on 9-6-2016 after completion and submission of investigation report by the election commission and, as such, the Rule is infructuous and it is not maintainable and therefore the Rule is liable to be discharged.

26. It is stated that the added respondent No. 11 filed an application on 7-5-2016 to the Chief Election Commissioner, Dhaka the copy of which was received by District Election Officer, Narsingdi at 1-00 PM of that day stating that the rival candidate Nuruzzaman and his cadre has forcefully entered into the vote center and shown off illegal arms and driven away the agents of the respondents No. 11 and sealed the ballot papers in favour of Boat (Nouka) (annexure-X (8).

27. The respondent No. 11 thereafter filed another application on 9-5-2016 to the Chief Election Commissioner, stating that election was held on 7-5-2016 in Choralia Union Parishad, Raypura, Narsingdi and there was huge rigging in center Nos. 6-9 wherein the casting vote was 100% in 2 (two) centres and 97.72% in another center it was 99.90% which is very much impossible and the same should be investigated by the election commission (annexure-X(9).

28. Some national daily newspapers published the said news on 12-5-2016, 14-5-2016, 15-5-2016 and 16-5-2016 in the Daily Ittefaq Prothom Alo, Kaler Knatha, Dainik Arthonitir Kagoj and Dainik Inkilab stating that the dead persons and the persons staying abroad cast votes in Choralia Union Parishad Election, Raypura, Narsingdi [(annexure-X (10)-X(15)].

29. The Election Commission thereafter took decision on 15-5-2016 to inquire the allegation of the said election held on 7-5-2016 and appointed one Mihir Sarwar Morshed, Regional Election Officer to investigate the matter upon proper inquiry of the registrar maintained in the Union Parishad and found that a good number of voters died before the election and their votes have been cast illegally and recommended to re-election.

30. Mr. Shafique Ahmed with Mr KB Rumy, the learned Advocates appearing for the petitioner submits that as per the Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2015 and the Local Government Union Parishad Rules, 2016 Rules there is no scope to file any complaint to the election commission by any candidate after completion of the election and declaration of the results by the Returning Officer and, as such, the impugned Memo No. ১৭.০০.৬৮৬৪.০৩৫.৪৬.০৯৩.১৪-২১৫ তারিখঃ ১৭-৫-২০১৬ signed by the respondent No. 4 containing an order of stay the publication of Gazette of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election held on 7-5-2016 of Raypura, Narsingdi and to conduct an investigation should be declared to have been without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

31. He again according to the Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2015, as well as, Rules, 2016 a complain can only be made before the election tribunal after completion of the election and all the other candidates must be made parties on the said complaint and the Tribunal shall pass formal judgment after hearing the parties and any aggrieved party can file appeal against the said judgment, but the said contesting candidate did not file any complaint before the Tribunal and, as such, the impugned memo dated 17-5-2016 containing an order of stay the publication of Gazette of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election held on 7-5-2016, Raypura, Narsingdi and to conduct an investigation is mala fide, arbitrary and illegal and should be declared to have made without law full authority and is of no legal effect.

32. He further submitted that as per Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2015, as well as, Rules, 2016 the Election Commission or any other body or tribunal or Court has no authority to stay the publication of Gazette of the result of the said election and, as such„ the impugned Memo No. ১৭.০০.৬৮৬৪.০৩৫.৪৬.০৯৩.১৪-২১৫ তারিখঃ ১৭-৫-২০১৬ signed by the respondent No. 4 containing an order of stay the publication of Gazette of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election held on 7-5-2016 of Raypura, Narsingdi and to conduct an investigation should be declared to have made without lawful and is of no legal effect.

33. Mr. Ahmed, again submitted as per provisions of the Rules, 2016 an applicant can only seek three remedies to the tribunal including cancellation of the election but even the Tribunal has no authority to stay the publication of Gazette of the result of the said election and, as such, the impugned memo dated 17-5-2016 containing an order of stay the publication of Gazette of the result of Choraralia Union Parishad Election held on 7-5-2016 of Raypura Union Parishad, Narsingdi and to conduct investigation should be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

34. He further agitated that the public functionaries must be vigilant, fair and duty bound in exercising the statutory power with which they are vested in for the public interest, but in the instant case the respondents willfully and deliberately have not acted in accordance with law, which is highly arbitrary and main fide and, as such, the impugned orders and judgment should be declared to have passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

35. Dr. Mohammed Yeasin Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 submits that in exercise of its jurisdiction under Article 119 of the Constitution of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh read with section 20 and 21 of the Local Government Union Parishad Act, 2009 and Rule 43 and 90 of the Local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 the Election commission is empowered with plenary power to conduct the Union Parishad election freely, fairly, justly and honestly which cover the entire process that starts with the publication of the notification of schedule and culminates with the publication of the result in the official gazette under section 21 of the Local government Union Parishad Act, read with and rule 43 of the local Government Union Parishad election Rules which allows the Election Commission in exercise of plenary power can act upon the post-election dispute.

36. He again submitted that on the basis of complain of the contesting chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman about illegalities and irregularities of voting in 4(four) election centres the Election Commission took decision to stay publication of the election result by Gazette notification and ordered Mihir Sawar Morshed, Regional Election Officer, Dhaka to hold inquiry and to submit report by 25-5-2016 vide impugned letter (annexure-E) and the Regional Election Officer, after recording statements and collecting information from the complainant, the petitioner, the Returning Officer, Members Candidates, Officer-in-Charge of Raypura Police Station, Officer-in-Charge of law enforcing agencies of the respective election centres, Upazila Nirbahi Officer of Raypura, Narsingdi District Election Officer of Narsingdi, and Upazila Election Officer of Raypura, Narsingdi has submitted his report to the election Commission Secre-tariat on 1-6-2016, from which it clearly appears that it was not possible to conduct a free, fair and impartial election according to the provisions of law, and rules in 4 (four) centres of Choraralia Union Parishad Election 2016 held on 7-5-2016.

37. He further submitted that during investigation the Regional Election Officer informed the petitioner and others and recorded their statements and collected information from them by open hearing on 22-5-2016, when the petitioner and his rival chairman candidate Mohammad Hasanuzzaman were duly present by signing in a printed sheet/form (annexure-5) and thereafter the Regional Election Officers submitted his report 1-6-2016 (annexure-4) but the petitioner suppressing such facts, after submissions of the investigation report, have filed the writ petition on 9-6-2016, therefore, the instant Rule is not maintainable.

38. Mr. Khan, again submitted that regarding the manner of poll held in four disputed centres of Chororalia Union Parishad General Election, on perusal of the investigation report of the Regional Election Officer, it appears that the Returning Officer, the Presiding Officers, Assistant Presiding Officers Polling Officers, and the Law enforcing agencies did not perform their duties properly and after stuffing votes by some persons, instead of stopping election process they continued election illegally and the votes of the contesting Chairman candidates were not counted and thus they miserably failed to conduct a free, fair and independent election according to law and procedure and, as such, the petition having being filed on 9-6-2016 suppressing facts of the power under Article 119(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh read with rule 90 of the local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, 2010 is quite competent to pass further order or orders and to review the decision of both the presiding and returning Officers on the basis of the merit of the investigation report. And in support of submission, he referred to the observations made in Abdur Rouf Minh vs Fazlur Rahman, 43 DLR (AD) 23, wherein it was observed inter alia that:

This is a question which cannot be determined except by recording evidence, given on oath. This is a job of the Tribunal and not of the Election Com-mission. The view of the Chief Election Commissioner that he is powerless to do anything in the absence of Rule 68 is not correct. The Election Commission has got power and jurisdiction to organise hold and conduct election fair and honest manner. But he is also subject to the Election Rules. Subject to this observation the petition is dismissed.

39. And he further referred to the observations made in Altaf Hussain vs Abul Kashem, 45 DLR (AD) 53; Mahmudul Haque vs Md Hedayetullah, 48 DLR (AD) 128; AKM Mayeedul Islam vs Bangladesh Election Commission, 48 DLR (AD) 208; Dr Mohiuddin Khan Alamgir vs Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, 62 DLR (AD) 425; and Ataur Rahman vs Election Commission, 20 BLT (AD) 99.

40. Mr. Md. Sagir Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 11 submits that this respondent filed application to the Election Commission and others just after the election stating that 4 centres are vulnerable and in those centres the petitioner in corruption, illegal activities and in collusion with the presiding officers cast votes in favour of the petitioner and 100% votes were cast in some centres against which this respondent made allegation of the rigging and accordingly the Election Commission after inquiry found that there was rigging in the election and took decision for re-election and there was no violation to stay the Gazette notification and re-election and, as such, the rule is liable to be discharged.

41. He further submitted that as per Rule 90 of the Local Government Union Parishad Election Rules, the Election Commission has special power to take decision of the election result as they think fit and proper and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged and he referred to the observation made in AFM Shah Alam vs Mujibul Huq, 41 DLR (AD) 68, wherein it was observed inter alia that:

Election Tribunal to hold trial of election petitions in accordance with procedure for trial of suits under Code of Civil Procedure-Tribunal's duties and functions stated in Rule 49.

42. On perusal of the submission of the learned Advocates of all the sides, the petition, affidavit-in-oppositions and the annexed documents the crux of the issue crystallises to the point as to whether the jurisdiction of the Election Tribunal will remain the same after publication of the result as “গণ বিজ্ঞপ্তি” (public notice) in Form ঠ, (ঠ-১) এবং (ঠ-২) as per Rule 42 of the “স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০১০”.

43. It is very evident to note that as per section 22 of the “স্থানীয় সরকার (ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ) নির্বাচন বিধিমালা, ২০০৯” which read as follows:

২২। নির্বাচনী দরখাস্তঃ(১)এই আইনের অধীনে অনুষ্ঠিত কোন নির্বাচন বা গৃহীত নির্বাচনী কায্যাক্রম বিষয়ে নির্বাচন ট্রাইব্যুনাল ব্যতীত কোন আদালত বা অন্য কোন কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আপত্তি উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না।

<u>44. On perusal of the law and the Rule it is very notable that an election is over when the result is published and it is made public through “গণ বিজ্ঞপ্তি” as per Rule 42 of the Rules, 2010 and the Rule 53 in that regard clearly embraces that any person those who are entitled to make an application with regard to an election can bring it before the Tribunal after publication of the official Gazette, as such, Rule 43 has prescribed the procedure and during the said period therefore in between publication of the result in Form ঠ, (ঠ-১) এবং (ঠ-২) and publication of the result in the official Gazette there is no forum for entertaining any allegation with regard to any election and/or any dispute. In the instant case the result was made public on 7-5-2016, therefore on completion of election. The Election Commission on receipt of the application from the respondent No. 11 through the impugned order dated 17-5-2016 ordered for any inquiry as well as for withholding the Gazette Notification.</u>

45. None of the provisions of the Act, 2009 or Rules, 2010 provides or empowers the Election Commission to withhold the Gazette Notification that would leave the parties at bay to bring election suit before the Tribunal as until publication of the official result the tribunal is not empowered to entertain any election dispute. Rule 19 as has been referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 11 clearly refers to the situations during ensuing election that is when the election is in the process, this provision does not attract the present case since the result has already been declared.

46. As such, we find that the application dated 9-5-2016 preferred by the respondent No. 11 before the Election Commission and its entertaining the same by passing the impugned order dated 17-5-2016 is done without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

47. It is also very much notable that the order passed by the Election Commission dated 17-5-2016 withholding the Gazette Notification and ordering an inquiry by 25-5-2016 by the Regional Election Officer is not supported by any reference to any law. It was observed in Ataur Rahman vs Election Commission represented by the Secretary, 15 BLC 506, wherein it was observed inter alia that:

On reading section 3 of Commission of Inquiry Act, 1956 it is crystal clear that only the Government is empowered to constitute a Commission of Inquiry. The Election Commission is a Constitutional independent body established under Article 118 of the Constitution and cannot be governed, controlled or supervised by the Government. Election Commission is not a substitute of the Government. The function of the Election Commission is to hold elections of all tires frees justly, honestly and in accordance with law and the Government acts as ancillary each other. Thus the Election Commission without any sanction of law constituted the Commission of Inquiry by Notification dated 24-3-2009 taking recourse of section 3 of the Commission of Inquiry Act, 1956 to inquire into the matters relating to election dispute. Government having realized the constitution of the Commission of Inquiry by the Election Commission was without any sanction of law gave post facto validation by the Gazette Notification dated 30-5-2009. By such giving post facto validation the illegality committed by the Election Commission in forming the Commission of Inquiry cannot be cured.

48. And it has already been discussed above that after declaration of result by the Returning Officer, the Election Commission is bound to do the Gazette Notification and its jurisdiction is culminated and any dispute with regard to the election is to be referred to the Election Tribunal.

49. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned letter being Memo No. 17.00. 68.64.035.46.093.14.215 dated 17-5-2016 signed by the respondent No. 4 is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

The respondent No. 2 is hereby directed to publish the Official Gazette with regard to result of the Chorarlia, Raypura, Narsingdi within 30 (thirty) days from the date of receipt of this judgment and order in accordance with law.

End.
